cards.english_meaning: the most important foundation of something
cards.extended_meaning: A cornerstone is something so important that a bigger system, belief, relationship, plan, or success depends on it. It is stronger than simply saying important; it means foundation-level important.
cards.core_idea: Something that supports a bigger thing at the foundation level.

content.short_meaning: the most important foundation of something
content.extended_recall_meaning: Use cornerstone when one value, principle, habit, system, or relationship is not just important, but foundational to a bigger result.

content.memory_trigger: A cornerstone holds the corner of a building; an abstract cornerstone holds a bigger idea together.
content.visual_scene: Imagine one strong stone supporting the corner of a building, and then imagine trust supporting a relationship in the same way.
content.memory_sentence: Trust is the cornerstone of a strong relationship.
content.recall_question: What word means the main foundation of a bigger system, value, or relationship?

sections.name: Notice
sections.content: Use cornerstone mostly for abstract foundations: values, principles, systems, strategies, policies, and relationships.

content.reason: Although cornerstone has a literal physical meaning, modern usage is mostly abstract: principles, values, strategies, systems, and relationships.

content.correct_tamil_speaker_usage: Tamil speakers can think of cornerstone as “முக்கிய அடித்தளம்”, not just “important thing.”
content.common_tamil_speaker_mistake: Hard work is a cornerstone for success.
content.correct_version: Hard work is a cornerstone of success.
content.translation_trap: Do not translate every “முக்கியமானது” as cornerstone. Cornerstone means foundation-level important, not just important.
content.thinking_difference: Tamil: “இது ரொம்ப முக்கியம்.” Natural English: “This is important.” Stronger English: “This is the cornerstone of the whole system.”

content.example_sentence: The cornerstone was laid in 1890.
Discipline is the cornerstone of success.
Free speech is a cornerstone of democracy.
Trust is the cornerstone of friendship.
Customer satisfaction is the cornerstone of our business.
Encryption is the cornerstone of secure communication.
Evidence is the cornerstone of scientific research.
Innovation is the cornerstone of our growth strategy.
Justice is a cornerstone of civil society.
Sleep is the cornerstone of feeling good.

unnatural_zones: Tiny details that are only mildly important
content.short_explanation: Use cornerstone when something is the deep foundation of a bigger thing, not just when something is useful.

commonly_used: Trust is the cornerstone of a healthy relationship.
Education is a cornerstone of social progress.
Security is the cornerstone of digital trust.
content.unnatural_example: This phone cover is the cornerstone of my phone.
content.natural_alternative: This phone cover is an important accessory.
content.explanation: Cornerstone is too strong for small details. It means foundation-level importance.

content.example: Honesty is the cornerstone of trust.
Exercise is a cornerstone of good health.
Clear communication serves as the cornerstone of teamwork.
Daily practice became the cornerstone of her progress.
Respect remains the cornerstone of their marriage.

content.rule: Use cornerstone when you want to say something is the main foundation of a bigger thing.
Do not use cornerstone for ordinary preferences or small details.
content.wrong: This phone cover is the cornerstone of my phone.
content.better: This phone cover is an important accessory.

content.usage_difference: Similar, often one of several supports

content.wrong: Hard work is a cornerstone for success.
content.correct: Hard work is a cornerstone of success.
content.reason: The natural pattern is cornerstone of, not cornerstone for.

content.wrong: This pen is the cornerstone of my bag.
content.correct: This pen is an important item in my bag.
content.reason: Cornerstone is too strong for ordinary objects.

sections.name: Paragraph-Based Real-Life Conversation / Story
sections.content: During a family discussion, Ravi said money was the most important part of a relationship. His sister disagreed and said, “Trust is the cornerstone of any strong relationship.” She did not mean trust was only useful; she meant the whole relationship depends on it. Later, Ravi used the same word at work: “Clear communication is the cornerstone of our team.” In both cases, cornerstone means the foundation that supports something bigger.

cards.english_meaning: to do something quickly or cheaply by skipping important steps
cards.extended_meaning: Cut corners means saving time, money, or effort in a way that lowers quality, safety, honesty, or care. It usually has a negative meaning.
cards.tamil_meaning: முக்கிய படிகளை தவிர்த்து சுலபமாக அல்லது மலிவாக செய்வது
cards.core_idea: You save effort by skipping steps that should not be skipped.

content.short_meaning: to skip important steps to save time or money
content.extended_recall_meaning: Use cut corners when someone finishes faster or cheaper by reducing quality, safety, or proper process.
content.memory_hint: cut corners = take a shortcut that damages quality

content.memory_trigger: Imagine someone literally cutting across the corner of a road instead of following the proper path.
content.visual_scene: A worker paints only the visible side of a wall and ignores the hidden side to finish quickly.
content.memory_sentence: Do not cut corners when safety is involved.
content.recall_question: What idiom means skipping important steps to save time or money?

sections.name: Notice
sections.content: Cut corners is usually negative. It suggests the person saved time, money, or effort in a way that reduced quality or safety.

content.reason: Although it has a possible literal image, modern daily use is mostly about skipping proper steps and lowering quality.

content.correct_tamil_speaker_usage: Think of cut corners as “சரியான முறையில் செய்யாமல் சுருக்கமாக செய்வது.”
content.common_tamil_speaker_mistake: I cut corners and arrived early.
content.correct_version: I took a shortcut and arrived early.
content.translation_trap: Do not use cut corners for every shortcut. Use it when the shortcut is careless or harmful.
content.thinking_difference: Tamil may use one idea for shortcut. English separates shortcut from cut corners.

content.example_sentence: The cyclist cut the corner and crossed the line.
content.note: Possible literal use, but the idiom is more common.

content.example_sentence: They cut corners to finish the renovation quickly.
You cannot cut corners with your health.
content.note: Natural when quality or care matters.

content.example_sentence: The cleaner cut corners and left dust under the sofa.
content.note: Very useful in home and daily-life complaints.

content.example_sentence: We should not cut corners during client onboarding.
The engineer refused to cut corners on safety checks.
content.note: Natural when standards or testing matter.

content.example_sentence: Researchers must not cut corners in data collection.
content.note: Acceptable, but more formal wording may be preferred.

content.example_sentence: The company cut corners to reduce production costs.
content.note: Very common in business and quality contexts.

content.example_sentence: The report suggests that the contractor cut corners.
content.note: Understandable in formal contexts, but slightly idiomatic.

content.example_sentence: Don't cut corners just because you are tired.

unnatural_zones: Situations where no quality or process is involved
content.short_explanation: Use cut corners when skipping steps creates risk, lower quality, or poor results.

commonly_used: Do not cut corners on safety.
They cut corners to save money.
The repair failed because someone cut corners.
not_normally_used: Good shortcuts that do not reduce quality
Small personal choices with no process
content.unnatural_example: I cut corners by taking a faster train.
content.natural_alternative: I saved time by taking a faster train.
content.explanation: Cut corners implies something improper or lower quality, not simply saving time.

content.example: They cut corners and the final result looked cheap.
Never cut corners on food safety.
He cut corners with the paperwork.
We avoided cutting corners during the move.
When you are tired, you may be tempted to cut corners.

content.rule: Use cut corners when someone skips important steps and the result may be worse, unsafe, unfair, or careless.
Do not use it for a smart shortcut that keeps quality high.
content.wrong: I cut corners by using a better app to finish faster.
content.better: I saved time by using a better app.

content.meaning: skip proper steps and reduce quality
do something too quickly and poorly

content.wrong: I cut corners and reached home faster.
content.correct: I took a shortcut and reached home faster.
content.reason: Cut corners is negative; taking a shortcut can be neutral.

content.wrong: They cut the corners in the report.
content.correct: They cut corners in the report.
content.reason: The idiom is cut corners, not cut the corners.

sections.name: Paragraph-Based Real-Life Conversation / Story
sections.content: When Meena hired someone to fix a leaking tap, the repair looked fine at first. Two days later, the leak returned. Her brother checked it and said, “They cut corners. They changed the outside part but ignored the real problem inside.” Meena understood that cutting corners is not just doing something quickly; it means skipping important steps and creating a poor result.
